top.line: My agents already run close to Holacracy; a new agent keeps the record, and only I ratify.
top.para: Ten of sixteen parts match strongly, two were missing (a Circle Rep and one record). holacracy.d's first chart: 15 sessions, two reporting outside their circle, $93.07 API-equivalent, five open proposals.

in-short.line: Roles not people; already in files; 10 of 16 strong; an agent keeps the record; one person ratifies; real tensions; rules suit software.

why.line: Holacracy writes the work down: roles with purpose, domains and accountabilities, in circles; tensions are the unit of change.
why.para: Why I like it, and the request to maestro.d on 22 November.

mapping.line: 10 strong, 4 partial, 2 missing: no Circle Rep and no single record of governance.
mapping.para: Part by part: rules, role files, grants as domains, conductors as leads, wakes as tactical meetings; the anchor, facilitation, governance cadence and records partial.

twins.line: A twin is one role filled on two accounts; the two writers avoid each other through a claims file.
twins.para: writer-10 on account B and newsroom.d on account D, never talking, never building at once.

record.line: holacracy.d keeps the governance record, writes proposals and changes nothing itself.
record.para: Its purpose, domain and accountabilities in Holacracy's terms; what it does not do; a script for the chart, the model only for proposals, no transcripts.

chart.line: 15 sessions on account D in four circles; sites.d and hub.d report to the maestro, not their circle's lead.
chart.para: The first tension, written as proposal 03; account B reported, not seen, and paused at the time.

cost.line: $93.07 API-equivalent across 14 sessions at one moment; the conductors and long-running roles cost most.
cost.para: Per-session spend as the record holds it, two sessions on a larger model than configured, and a simulation finding work concentrating.

ratify.line: Only I ratify; agents never widen their own grants. Five proposals are open.
ratify.para: The main difference from Holacracy, and the first five proposals, including one sentence of purpose only I can write.

software.line: People tire of Holacracy's rules; agents read every rule at every wake, and the cost moves to tokens.
software.para: Fortune on Zappos in 2016, and the remaining risk of process for its own sake.

limits.line: One agent's analysis; account B not seen; one moment's costs; secondary Zappos figures; a simulation; nothing decided.

sources.line: maestro.d's analysis, holacracy.d's brief, record and proposals, the constitution, Fortune and arXiv, read 22 November 2026.
